question: A set of positive numbers has the triangle property if it has three distinct elements that are the lengths of the sides of a triangle whose area is positive. Consider sets $\{4, 5, 6, \ldots, n\}$ of consecutive positive integers, all of whose ten-element subsets have the triangle property. What is the largest possible value of $n$?
solution:
Write a ten-element subset in increasing order as a₁ < ⋯ < a₁₀. For each k ≥ 3, the largest sum of two elements smaller than aₖ is aₖ₋₂ + aₖ₋₁. A positive-area triangle with largest side aₖ exists exactly when this sum exceeds aₖ. Thus the subset has no triangle exactly when aₖ ≥ aₖ₋₂ + aₖ₋₁ for every k ≥ 3.
To minimize the last element of a triangle-free subset, start with the smallest possible entries, 4 and 5, and take each later entry equal to the sum of its predecessors. This gives 4, 5, 9, 14, 23, 37, 60, 97, 157, 254. By induction, every triangle-free subset has each entry at least as large as the corresponding entry in this list. Hence none fits when n = 253, while the list itself is a triangle-free subset for every n ≥ 254.
Final answer: 253
